messages.author: 7d2a96af532ed7de
messages.subject: Dynamically Generating Static Web Pages..?
parts:
Hello All,

I'm thinking about building a little website where some basic data and jazzy charts are displayed in a standard format, for 100s of different entries in a database. There wouldn't need to be any 'live' analysis. Like building a website long the lines of Wikipedia or IMDB, but with lots of snazzy .js visualisations (thanks to Ramnath!).

I'm keen to use R because of the stats & visualisation capabilities, but mainly because I know R and I'm lazy :)

In terms of how users would place a burden on the server, I get the impression that performance (for fixed cost) would be much better if I could dynamically generate static pages (say once a day, or when new information comes in) which could be stored, served, and connected with managed hyperlinks - as opposed to create a single page app where each user was constantly dynamically generating pages in their own R session. I'm not quite sure what the terminology is for the two approaches.

My hunch is that the sensible answer is "learn Python, and try it's huge web frameworks", but as a dunce R programmer, is there any (even nasty, hacky) way to do this with Shiny? Is this sort of functionality being talked about or planned for the future? Although I haven't read anything about it on the lists, it seems to relate to markdown and Yihui's work (and this post).

If not, if anyone's been successful tackling a similar problem, I'd be keen to know how the approached it!

Apologies for the kind of off topic/ill-formed question,

Brendan

parts: You could leverage Shiny's HTML builder library for this if you wanted to. But I'd take a closer look at doing it with knitr, rapport, and clickme rather than Shiny if you really want to do static page generation.
